source: reference library, each distinct program once, rules labelled per part; cited as <program file>:<line>

told.words: N MM UNTERLAGE // IN Y- (or X-, Y+...)
told.meaning: A spacer N mm thick in the jaw on that side, pushing the part N mm away from that jaw. Not the parallels under the part.
The part is N mm in X and N mm in Y. 50 IN X/Y, 50 x 50 mm, is one of the standard sizes of the top plates.

rules.rule: Every line but "%" and the O line carries an N number, N1, N2, N3... in steps of 1 (FANUC: N9999 repeated after line 9,999).

rules.label: majority

rules.rule: HAAS programs start with the safety line "G40 G17 G53 G49 G80 G90".
rules.label: majority

rules.rule: FANUC programs start with "G0 G53 G49 Z0 G94 M95" (retract, cancel the length offset, feed per minute).
rules.label: consistent across the library

rules.rule: Each tool change is announced by the operation name: a "(TOOLPATH NAME)" comment right before "T.. M6". An operation that goes on with the same tool is a comment "(NAME MIT WERKZEUG <tool code>)" instead.
rules.label: majority

rules.rule: After "T.. M6" the tool is described: "(NAME / CODE)" with a code like SF_10.00_030_000_AL, then "(DIAMETER d MM/LENGTH l MM)".
rules.label: majority

rules.rule: HAAS: the length offset is "G00 G43 H<tool> Z.." with H the number of the tool in the spindle.
rules.label: majority

rules.rule: FANUC: the length offset is "G00 G43 Z.. H#513 D#513 M254": the offset number comes from #513.
rules.label: consistent across the library

rules.rule: The length offset brings the tool to Z50. (50 mm above program zero) before anything else.
rules.label: minority

rules.rule: The coolant comes on with the length offset: M08 on the G43 line.
rules.label: majority

rules.rule: The spindle starts on the positioning move right after the G43 line: "G00 G90 X.. Y.. S.. M03".
rules.label: majority

rules.rule: Drilling and tapping cycles return to the start height (G98), never to R (G99).
rules.label: consistent across the library

rules.rule: The R plane of a cycle is R2. (2 mm above Z0); lower R planes are written where the hole starts lower.
rules.label: majority

rules.rule: The drilling cycles are G81, G83 (always with a peck Q) and G84 (tapping); G73 is never used.
rules.label: consistent across the library

rules.rule: Holes are spot drilled, drilled and tapped with canned cycles, never long-hand with G01 moves.
rules.unit: spot drilling, drilling and tapping operations
rules.label: consistent across the library

rules.rule: Arcs are written with I and J (centre), not with R.
rules.label: consistent across the library

rules.rule: No subprograms or macros: the only call is the FANUC table out "M98 P7999" (#513 in the FANUC G43 lines is a value the control holds, not a macro).
rules.label: majority

rules.rule: Every motion line carries its motion code (G00, G01, G02, G03), also when it does not change. Not the moves into a drilling cycle (the drop to the R height, the move to the next hole between two cycles): they go on from the G00 before them. Inside a cycle the lines are hole positions. Machine moves (G53, such as the table out G53 Y0) are not counted: they are written without one.
rules.label: majority

rules.rule: A straight move writes only the axes that change: a word repeating the current position is left out. Not the first moves of an operation (the spindle-start line, the first Z move), which state the position in full; arcs write their end point in full.
rules.label: majority

rules.rule: The feed is written only when it changes (after a tool change or a cycle it is written again).
rules.label: majority

rules.rule: Coordinates (X Y Z I J R) are written short: no trailing zeros after the point (X10.5, X10.), no leading zero before it (Z-.6), except the G52 lines (three decimals). Tool numbers after H are zero-padded on HAAS (H03).
rules.label: majority

rules.rule: Whole-number feeds: HAAS writes them with a dot (F3000.), FANUC without (F3000).
rules.label: consistent across the library

rules.rule: HAAS programs end with "G0 G53 G49 Y0 Z0 M89" (table out, length offset cancelled, through-spindle coolant off), the machining time comment and M30.
rules.label: majority

rules.rule: FANUC programs end with the table out "M98 P7999" and M30.
rules.label: majority

rules.rule: The header names the part, its material and finished size, and the saw-cut blank: "(NAME MATERIAL / AxBxC / ZUSCHNITT:DxExF)".
rules.label: majority

rules.rule: Every clamping is announced to the operator: M0 stops with the clamping notes right before its G52.
rules.label: consistent across the library

rules.rule: In the first clamping program zero is either 2 mm inside the X-/Y+ corner of the raw block ("G52 X-48. Y48.") or the centre of the block as clamped.
rules.label: majority

rules.rule: When the first zero is on a corner, it is 2 mm inside the raw faces: "G52 X-48. Y48.".
rules.label: majority

rules.rule: Program Z0 is at least 46 mm above the vise floor (G52 Z of -11 or higher): with 45 mm jaws, at least 1 mm of the part stands above them.
rules.label: consistent across the library

rules.rule: In the vise the part is gripped at least 3 mm deep: it stands on parallels of 42 mm or less in the 45 mm jaws.
rules.label: consistent across the library

rules.rule: Without a spacer, a cut beside the clamped faces (Y) stops above the jaw top, mostly 1 to 2 mm above it: the part is set high enough for its outside contour.
rules.unit: vise clampings with such a cut and no spacer
rules.label: consistent across the library

rules.rule: A spacer between the part and a jaw ("15 MM ZWISCHENLAGE IN Y-", "15 MM UNTERLAGE // IN Y-") frees that side: cuts beside that face go below the jaw top.
rules.unit: vise clampings with a spacer at Y- or Y+
rules.label: consistent across the library

rules.rule: The first clamping removes the most material (in the simulation).
rules.unit: programs with two clampings or more
rules.label: majority

rules.rule: The second clamping turns the part over: 180° about X or about Y.
rules.unit: programs with two clampings or more
rules.label: majority

rules.rule: The part lies with its longer side along X, along the jaws.
rules.label: majority

rules.rule: Each program starts by facing the top (PLAN / MESSERKOPF) in its first clamping.
rules.label: majority

rules.rule: A clamping that turns the part over starts by facing its new top (the part is brought to thickness).
rules.label: majority

rules.rule: A clamping that stands the part on an edge (a quarter turn) does not face.
rules.label: consistent across the library

rules.rule: Chamfering and deburring (FASE / ENTGRATEN) come last in their clamping.
rules.label: majority

rules.rule: Within a clamping: face, spot drill, drill, tap; then pockets, contours, finishing and counterbores (in any order among them); chamfers and deburring last. Holes come before milling: of the 166 clampings with both, 132 make all their holes first, 7 all their milling first.
rules.label: majority

rules.rule: In a clamping that roughs (pockets, contours) and finishes (SCHLICHT), its last finishing pass comes after its first roughing one. (Which roughing each finishing pass belongs to is not read.)
rules.label: majority

rules.rule: A pre-facing pass (VORPLAN) is followed by a final facing pass (FERTIGPLAN) in the same clamping.
rules.label: consistent across the library

rules.rule: A hole drilled under 4 mm is spot drilled first (ZENTRIER / NC-ANBOHREN, same clamping); from 4 mm up it is drilled without spot drilling. 4 mm is the size that best separates the library's holes.
rules.label: majority

rules.rule: A tapped hole is drilled first (the core hole), in the same clamping.
rules.label: consistent across the library

rules.rule: Holes are drilled with G83 and a peck, whatever their depth; G81 is for spot drilling only.
rules.label: consistent across the library

rules.rule: Tools are named by a code TYPE_D.DD_LLL_GGG_MAT (a copy carries a number after it, "_1"): type (MK face mill, SF end mill, SB drill, ZB or AB spot drill, GB tap, ST chamfer/graver...), diameter, length, and the material its data is for.
rules.label: majority

rules.rule: The tool's cutting data is for the part's material: the code's material is the header's.
rules.label: majority

byType.rule: Every clamping is announced to the operator: M0 stops with the clamping notes right before its G52.

The second clamping turns the part over: 180° about X or about Y.
The part lies with its longer side along X, along the jaws.

A clamping that turns the part over starts by facing its new top (the part is brought to thickness).
A clamping that stands the part on an edge (a quarter turn) does not face.
Chamfering and deburring (FASE / ENTGRATEN) come last in their clamping.

A pre-facing pass (VORPLAN) is followed by a final facing pass (FERTIGPLAN) in the same clamping.

A tapped hole is drilled first (the core hole), in the same clamping.
Holes are drilled with G83 and a peck, whatever their depth; G81 is for spot drilling only.

Tools are named by a code TYPE_D.DD_LLL_GGG_MAT (a copy carries a number after it, "_1"): type (MK face mill, SF end mill, SB drill, ZB or AB spot drill, GB tap, ST chamfer/graver...), diameter, length, and the material its data is for.
